## Overview

Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate, rather than letting an unbounded buffer grow until the process runs out of memory.

## Common Implementations

### Bounded Queues
The producer is blocked once the queue reaches capacity, preventing unbounded memory growth. This is a passive mechanism where the producer cannot emit further items until the consumer drains the queue.

### Credit-Based Flow Control
The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items. The producer tracks remaining credits and stops emitting once credits are exhausted, waiting for the consumer to issue new credits as it processes items.

### Reactive-Pull Models
Instead of the producer pushing items at its own pace, the consumer requests items on its own schedule. This gives the consumer direct control over the emission rate and is sometimes called a "pull-based" or "on-demand" model.

## Significance

Backpressure is critical for systems handling variable load or where consumer speed may fluctuate. Without backpressure, fast producers can exhaust system memory by filling buffers faster than slow consumers can drain them, leading to out-of-memory errors or system crashes.
